extracted.intended_audience: students, teachers, and general readers interested in mathematical problem solving and heuristics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on heuristic methods for discovering proofs and solving mathematical problems (and applying those methods to other reasoning problems). Emphasizes focusing on essentials, working around obstacles, and using sustained attention/insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical method as a general problem-solving tool
rubrics_metrics.description: The mathematical method of demonstrating a proof or finding an unknown can be of help in attacking any problem that can be 'reasoned' out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book claims applicability beyond pure mathematics — examples include building a bridge and winning a game of anagrams; treat mathematical-style reasoning and structure as tools that transfer to other domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strip away irrelevancies and go to the heart of the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Stripping away irrelevancies and going straight to the heart of a problem is a key instruction for solving problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the core elements of the problem; eliminate distracting details that do not affect the solution. The text emphasizes learning to identify what is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use heuristics — the art and science of discovery and invention
rubrics_metrics.description: How to Solve It popularized heuristics, the art and science of discovery and invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and apply general problem-solving strategies (heuristics) rather than relying solely on rote methods; heuristics are presented as teachable and central to successful problem solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcome difficulties by going around them
rubrics_metrics.description: “My method to overcome a difficulty is to go around it.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When blocked on a direct approach, seek indirect routes or transform the problem so the obstacle disappears; use alternative perspectives or auxiliary constructions instead of forcing a stuck approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't overtrust diagrams — reason correctly from imperfect figures
rubrics_metrics.description: “Geometry is the science of correct reasoning on incorrect figures.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that working figures or diagrams may be imperfect; focus on sound logical reasoning rather than literal interpretation of a drawing. Use diagrams as guides but validate conclusions by rigorous argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sustained attention/immersion to trigger insight
rubrics_metrics.description: “In order to solve this differential equation you look at it till a solution occurs to you.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for problems to incubate; sustained examination and mental engagement can bring sudden insight. Persistence and prolonged contemplation are legitimate problem-solving tactics.
